page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The system is equipped with 32 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, measured via stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests, falls within the average range. Memory performance is highlighted by a strong PassMark memory score, though raw memory bandwidth for large-block read and write operations remains average. The instance also demonstrates strong text generation speeds during small-model LLM inference, alongside average performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance type provides a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not demand large memory footprints. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it highly specialized for pure processing tasks. It is well-suited for workloads such as software compilation, batch processing, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference.
